Rail collision: signal box recordings released

By a staff reporter in Port Avery, with additional reporting

Recordings released on Thursday reveal the conversations between two train drivers and the signal box in the minutes before Wednesday's collision outside Port Avery.

In the first recording, a signaller can be heard telling the driver of the northbound service that the line ahead is clear, and that he may proceed at normal speed.

Less than a minute later, the same signaller warns a second driver, travelling south on the same track, to stop at once, but the warning comes too late, investigators say.

The regional transport minister said the recordings would be studied by the accident board, which has promised an interim report within a month.

What the recordings show

The board said the timing of the two instructions, about fifty seconds apart, was the focus of its inquiry, alongside the state of the signalling equipment.

Unions representing signal staff said their members had raised concerns about the equipment, which dates from the 1980s, on several occasions this year.

Services on the line are expected to remain suspended until at least next week, the operator said, with replacement buses running between the affected stations.
